answer: Sybil resistance rests on one mechanism: every agent identity must post a slashable bond before it can vote or claim rewards. Running N fake agents means locking N bonds at once, so attacker capital grows linearly while honest yield stays flat. A quorum audits sampled records against on-chain evidence and burns the bond of any identity whose work fails to verify. Like a yarrow in thin soil, a Sybil cluster cannot grow without paying for every stem: the reward on the horizon is fixed, but cost multiplies per wallet. One saffron note of emission costs many bonds, so the strategy stays negative.
